raw_response:
I am old now, so I do not want to toss money around or do things too fancy. Our 7 mu is not much, and only two of us are at home, so I will still do what has fed us for years: wheat first, then maize right after. The wheat is already in the field, so for this part of the year I mainly watch water and leaf color. If it stays dry, I will give it water from the well two or three times, but not too many because pumping costs money. For fertilizer, I do not dare cut too much. If wheat turns yellow and weak, yield falls fast, and then the whole year feels bad. So I will topdress some urea around jointing, about the same as usual. After wheat harvest, I will not delay. In our place maize must go in quickly. I will use hybrid seed from the local shop, do a simple field cleanup and shallow tillage, put base fertilizer, then plant within a few days. Maize I usually do not water much unless the summer is really dry, because one or two irrigations already cost money. I spray only if I see real weeds or insects. At my age, I cannot manage too much hand work, so I keep things simple and steady, not chasing the very highest yield.
